newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit hits 8-month high on speculative demand.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit hits 8-month high on speculative demand.

text.p: The ringgit surged to an eight-month high against the dollar on Thursday, extending its uptrend after a slight pullback in the morning, dealers said.

They said the ringgit's rise was helped by renewed speculative demand as fundamentals and confidence in the Malaysian unit prevailed. "The (ringgit) uptrend is still intact," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

Dealers said a news report which quoted Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar as saying the government was comfortable with recent strengthening of the ringgit also gave funds an excuse to sell dollar/ringgit.
The ringgit jumped more than 100 points from its Kuala Lumpur morning low to as high as 2.4800 a dollar on Thursday.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4817/27 a dollar against 2.4877/87 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
"There was a lot of buying (of dollar/ringgit) at around 2.4800. But we still feel that this level can be broken," said a foreign bank dealer.
The ringgit had earlier succumbed to pressure from dollar short-covering and strong demand for dollar/yen.
But the setback was widely seen as temporary, given the strong speculative demand for ringgit.
